question.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{3}⁡(2x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ {v}^{′}=9{x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,v=\int 9{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x=3{x}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 9{x}^{2}{log}_{3}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{3}⁡(2x)\cdot (3{x}^{3})-\int \frac{3{x}^{3}}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{x}^{3}{log}_{3}⁡(2x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int 3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{x}^{3}{log}_{3}⁡(2x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\cdot {x}^{3}+C \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{3}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$
